Bit brief, but a good video on Heidegger

Heidegger says that the authentic is not to be preferred to the inauthentic. But, the words themselves seem to suggest what is said in the video. That reading or understanding of Heidegger, a well known error, is due to an inauthentic attitude, which, naturally, places special value on the authentic (i.e., the spiritual or the wise way). Heidegger's point is to show the range, not to moralize or prescribe one position over the other. The practice is sometimes referred to as hermeneutic phenomonology.
What is the coolest thing you've ever seen or done on the internet?

Just discovering the internet when I was 15 (yeah I'm old). I grew up in a small french city and I felt like I was different, I didn't belonged. I was probably the only "nerd" in a 30km radius lol. The internet was the portal that showed me there was a world of awesomess out there that I could reach. People that were like me. It really gave a new meaning to my life.

I still think, although I was not part of it, and it had it's failures that Project Chanology was one of the most impressive things I've seen emerge from the internet, setting the standard really for protests.

The internet had been edging toward that for years beforehand with things seeping into real life and the lines blurring, but that was the point I think when a lot of onlookers realised the power that the internet can have in real life. A massive worldwide, movement of people galvanized as a result of an action taken on the internet, and organised through the internet onto the streets.

Still really cool today
